# ATS Resume Toolkit (cv.shykov.dev)

> A free, open-source ATS resume checker that runs entirely in the browser. It
> scores a PDF or DOCX resume for applicant-tracking-system readability, matches
> it against a job description, and exports an ATS-clean PDF. No file upload, no
> account, no LLM call, no tracking.

## What it does

- **Analyze** — drop a PDF or DOCX and get a 0–100 ATS score with the
  highest-impact fixes ranked first. The rubric is fixed and published:
  25 points parseability, 15 contact details, 35 sections, 15 formatting,
  10 content signals.
- **Job-description match** — paste a job ad and see which of its keywords the
  resume already covers and which are missing.
- **Writing style check** — flags stock phrasing, monotone sentence rhythm,
  repeated bullet openers, vague claims with no number, and heavy passive
  voice. It is explicitly *not* an AI-text detector: that needs a language
  model, and published detectors misfire on writing by non-native English
  speakers.
- **Build** — a form that produces an ATS-clean PDF with a live score.

## How it differs from other ATS checkers

- The resume never leaves the device. Parsing (pdf.js, mammoth) and scoring both
  run as client-side JavaScript; there is no backend that could receive a file.
- Scoring is deterministic, not generative. The same resume always yields the
  same score, and no model call sits behind the interface.
- No account, no email wall, no paid tier, no upsell.
- MIT-licensed and auditable — the scoring rules, parser, and export path are
  all readable in the public repository.

## Limits worth stating

- An ATS score is a heuristic for machine readability. It is not a prediction of
  whether a human recruiter will shortlist the resume.
- Image-only (scanned) PDFs carry no extractable text, so page-count and
  parseability signals are unreliable for them.
- No résumé is scored against any specific vendor's ATS; the checks target the
  parsing behaviour those systems have in common.
